messages:
Maya: Heads-up — BlueHarbor asked for an "edge" instruct variant: instruction-tuned fork of v4-base, 100k context, and aggressive quantization experiments (int8/int4). They want a rapid intake and rough prioritization by EOD.
Sam: Got it. What's the business ask / SLA?
Maya: They have a compliance workflow and need deterministic summaries for legal reviews. Target: 99.5% availability, median p95 latency <= 450ms for 2k prompt, and cost <= 0.6x current hosted unit. Revenue impact small but strategic (security partner).
Lee: Do they require private deployment or hosted?
Maya: Private (VPC) ideally, but will accept Dedicated if timing forces it. Data residency in EU.
Toni: Important to split scope: (1) Bring-up base instruct variant w/ 64k -> verify correctness. (2) Long-context 100k engineering (KV cache + chunking tests). (3) Quant sweep (fp16 -> int8 -> int4) with quality/regression checks.
Raj: Proposed owners: Lee -> infra/private deploy; Toni -> quant experiments; Maya -> customer comms & acceptance criteria; Sam -> prioritization + business sign-off.
Sam: Prioritization: recommend P2. Not top revenue but partner strategic. Can we estimate engineering days?
Toni: Rough: base instruct quick-tune (3d), eval harness + smoke tests (2d), quant sweep + QAT-ish fine-tune (5-7d), 100k infra work (7-10d). Total parallelizable parts: ~2 weeks if staffed.
Maya: Customer requested a checklist. I'll drop a first pass, please edit: 
- Confirm license & weights (open model variant)
- Create tenant variant config (model_id, instruct_head checkpoint)
- Small instruct fine-tune (100k tokens curated prompts)
- Run eval suite: instruction-following, summarization, hallucination, instruction-robustness
- Latency/throughput baseline on Dedicated hardware
- Quantization sweep (fp16 -> int8 -> int4) with eval gating
- Long-context engineering: KV cache sizing, prefix caching, chunked tokenization tests
- Security/compliance review (EU data residency)
- Canary rollout + smoke production tests

Lee: I'll add infra specifics. For private we need model packaging + KMS notes. Also check kernel selection for >64k sequences.
Toni: Quant config sample for initial sweep: 
```
model_variant: blueharbor-instruct-v1
quant_modes: ["fp16","int8","int4"]
int8_params: { per_channel: true, clip: 0.01 }
int4_params: { qtype: "nf4", block_size: 128 }
rollout_policy: { canary: 5%, fallback: v4-base }
```
Maya: Nice. Key acceptance criteria from customer: 
- BLEU/ROUGE-ish not enough; they want instruction accuracy on 200 blind legal prompts >= 92% pass rate.
- No material regression vs hosted baseline on hallucination benchmarks.
- Throughput target of >= 80 tokens/s on their Dedicated SKU.

eval-bot: Automated eval run queued on branch blueharbor/instruct-quicktune. Expected ETA: 3h.
Sam: Should we require human-in-the-loop eval on first canary? I recommend yes for legal edge cases.
Maya: Agreed. We'll schedule SME review during canary.
Raj: Any red flags? Quant int4 can be risky for instruction fidelity. We should gate int4 behind a human-reviewed regression threshold.
Toni: Agreed. Proposed gating: int8 allowed if metric drop <= 2 points; int4 allowed only if drop <= 1 point AND no new hallucination classes.
Lee: Scheduling note: private infra changes may take extra 48h for infra ticket and customer approvals.
deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1228: "BlueHarbor private deploy prep - kernel + KMS" assigned to Lee. ETA 3d.
Maya: Next steps: Toni start quant sweep branch, Lee start infra ticket, Raj draft customer acceptance checklist doc, Sam confirm prioritization with Rev Ops. I'll update BlueHarbor tomorrow.
Toni: Starting sweep now, will post short results here.
Maya: Thanks — keep updates short and tag when canary ready. :thumbsup:
